topic: Sleep deprivation effects on the body
hook: What happens to your body without sleep
caption:
After about 17 hours awake, your brain can perform roughly like it does at 0.05% blood alcohol. Most people hit that point on a normal late night.

Skip sleep for longer and your hunger hormones shift, microsleeps creep in, and your brain's overnight cleaning shift gets cut short. Sources: Williamson & Feyer 2000, Spiegel et al. 2004, Xie et al. 2013 (Science).

What's the longest you've ever stayed awake?

1/5 17 hours awake (17 h)
After about 17 hours awake, your reaction speed and accuracy can match someone at 0.05% blood alcohol.
🎨 AI-generated image

2/5 Microsleeps take over
Your brain starts switching off for seconds at a time, even with your eyes open, often without you noticing.
📷 PattayaPatrol (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

3/5 Hunger hormones flip (+28%)
After two short nights, hunger hormone ghrelin rose 28% and fullness hormone leptin fell 18% in one study.
🎨 AI-generated image

4/5 Brain cleaning stops (60%)
Sleep helps fluid wash waste out of the brain. In mice, the space between brain cells grew about 60% during sleep.
📷 Edeh Sophia (CC0) via wikimedia

5/5 The 264-hour record (264 h)
In 1964, a student stayed awake for 11 days. Guinness later stopped tracking the record because it is dangerous.
